note: Machine-checkable closure ledger. Every row carries a predicate that returns true when the defect is PRESENT at HEAD. `node scripts/check-bottlenecks.mjs` fails when a row marked `closed` still fires (REOPENED), when a row marked `open` no longer fires (FIXED_UNRECORDED), or when a row marked `refuted` fires (REFUTED_BUT_PRESENT). Rows here replace the prose findings list: a claim that cannot be machine-checked is a row with `kind: "manual"`, which is re-verified rather than trusted. Never delete a `refuted` row — it is what stops a dead finding from being re-derived.

rows.title: The 2026-09-18 `gpu-process` P0 fault (`electron.exe+0x897d241`) is unattributed and unowned
rows.evidence: The 4 P0 `runtime.process` rows written by crash-report-intake.ts:104-160 from real Crashpad dumps. Three browser-process `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` `read of 0x0` faults (`electron.exe+0x684d7a8` @ 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17, `+0x27340e3` @ 2026-09-16) are mitigated at HEAD by inspection: `safeEnableDeviceEmulation` returns early when `!this.isTabViewAttached(view)` (src/main/browser/native-tab-host.ts:709-736). The 2026-09-18 `gpu-process` fault at `+0x897d241` is not addressed by that guard, cannot be re-symbolized here (no Chromium PDB symbol server), and carries no accepted-with-fallback disposition — so it reads as an open P0 with no owner. Recorded from the 2026-09-19 Core Issue audit (report section 6, item 5).

predicate.reVerifyWith: re-symbolize the 2026-09-18 dump against a Chromium PDB set, or record an explicit accepted-with-fallback disposition on the intake row

rows.title: The capture-timeout census counts a paused-but-buffered element as playing, and offers a remedy that cannot clear its own predicate
rows.evidence: CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_PROBE_EXPRESSION (src/main/tools/browser-control-port.ts:1198-1204) counts an element as playing when `el.paused === false || el.readyState > 2`, so a paused video that finished buffering reads as playing; it surfaces as `N playing media element(s)` (push at :2388) with `Remedy: anti.media.freeze(tabId)`. Observed live 2026-09-19: the two videos were `{readyState: 4, paused: true}` while the error claimed '2 playing media element(s) (video x2)', and anti.media.freeze pauses media — it never lowers readyState, so it cannot clear the predicate it is offered for. With the media removed from the DOM the same capture still timed out, with no diagnosis clause at all, while the real condition was a tab whose view had no compositor surface (`attached: false` while the toolbar showed it as the active tab; frames and lazy images resumed once the tab was re-presented). Recorded from the 2026-09-19 Core Issue audit (report section 9).

predicate.reVerifyWith: take the live capture-timeout message on a stalled tab; close when `playing` counts only `paused === false`, a distinct `buffered` count exists, the freeze remedy is attached only to the former, and a clean census names the no-compositor-surface cause
